# windows_volume (Resource)

Formats one partition on a data disk on a remote Windows host via SSH and PowerShell (`Format-Volume` / `Get-Volume` / `Set-Volume`) and manages its volume label.

Identity is the Get-Volume UniqueId (the `\\?\Volume{...}\` object path). The hosting `partition_id` is the `windows_partition` ID (`<disk_unique_id>|<guid>` on GPT, `<disk_unique_id>|<offset>` on MBR). Formatting destroys the partition's data: a partition that already carries a file system is refused with `already_formatted` unless `allow_format_existing` is set, and the boot/system/EFI/MSR/recovery/pagefile guard fails closed with `protected_storage`.

Deleting the resource only drops the adoption from state and makes no remote call: the volume and its data are left exactly as they are (volumes are never unformatted). Consider `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` for volumes holding data.

Typical layering is `windows_disk` → `windows_partition` → `windows_volume` (#292): adopt and initialize the disk, carve the partition, then format it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Minimal example: format the carved data partition to NTFS with a label.
# Formatting destroys the partition's data: a partition that already carries
# a file system is refused with `already_formatted` unless
# `allow_format_existing` is set, and protected partitions fail closed with
# `protected_storage`.
resource "windows_volume" "data" {
  partition_id      = windows_partition.data.id
  file_system       = "NTFS"
  file_system_label = "TFDATA"
}

# Advanced example: exFAT with an explicit allocation unit size and a slow
# full format (which scans for bad sectors). Deleting the resource only drops
# the adoption from state: the volume and its data are left untouched.
# Consider `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` for volumes holding data.
resource "windows_volume" "backup" {
  partition_id         = windows_partition.data.id
  file_system          = "exFAT"
  file_system_label    = "BACKUP"
  allocation_unit_size = 131072 # 128 KiB

  full_format = true

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `file_system` (String) File system to format the partition with: `NTFS`, `ReFS`, `exFAT` or `FAT32` (case-insensitive, stored in canonical form). ForceNew: changing it reformats the volume and destroys its data (plan warns).
- `partition_id` (String) Hosting partition in `<disk_unique_id>|<guid_or_offset>` form (the `id` of a `windows_partition` resource: the GUID on GPT disks, the byte offset on MBR disks). ForceNew: a different partition is a different volume.

### Optional

- `allocation_unit_size` (Number) Allocation unit (cluster) size in bytes, set at format time only. ForceNew. Null (default) selects the host default. Must be a power of two between 512 and 2097152, further narrowed per file system: NTFS 512-65536, FAT32 512-32768, exFAT 512-2097152, ReFS 4096 or 65536 only.
- `allow_format_existing` (Boolean) Permit formatting a partition that already carries a file system (reformatting destroys its data). Without it, formatting an already-formatted partition is an `already_formatted` error suggesting import instead.
- `file_system_label` (String) Volume label, enforced in place (`Set-Volume -NewFileSystemLabel`; empty clears it). Null (unset) leaves the observed label unmanaged. Length limits depend on the file system: 32 characters for NTFS/ReFS, 11 for exFAT/FAT32.
- `full_format` (Boolean) Perform a full format (which scans for bad sectors) instead of the default quick format. A full format can take a long time on large disks; the resource timeouts default to 30m to cover it.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `drive_letter` (String) Assigned drive letter (upper-cased), as observed on the host. Empty when the volume has none; manage it with the `drive_letter` of `windows_partition`.
- `drive_type` (String) Get-Volume DriveType (e.g. Fixed), as observed on the host.
- `health_status` (String) Get-Volume HealthStatus (e.g. Healthy), as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier; the Get-Volume UniqueId of the formatted volume.
- `operational_status` (String) Get-Volume OperationalStatus (e.g. OK), as observed on the host.
- `path` (String) Get-Volume Path (the `\\?\Volume{...}\` object path), as observed on the host.
- `size_bytes` (Number) Get-Volume Size in bytes, as observed on the host.
- `size_remaining_bytes` (Number) Get-Volume SizeRemaining in bytes, as observed on the host.

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing volume by its Get-Volume UniqueId.
terraform import windows_volume.data '\\?\Volume{11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555}\'

# Import an existing volume by drive letter (the trailing colon is optional).
terraform import windows_volume.data 'E:'
```
